prerequisites: Ability to write medium-complexity programs using the C programming language

learning_outcomes.text: Know and understand the operating mechanisms of the Linux/Unix operating system.
Know and understand the methods for process management and inter-process communication in the Linux operating system.
Be able to program an application using correctly the basic tools provided by operating systems.
Be able to program complex applications, for example with modular or client-server architectures, by exploiting Linux operating system's inter-process communication techniques.

Be able to autonomously understand technical documentation made available by operating system developer communities and major software companies, with particular reference to open source systems based on Linux.

syllabus_topics: Inter-process communication in Linux: unnamed pipes (6 hours)
Inter-process communication in Linux: named pipes (6 hours)
assessment_rules: Learning is assessed through practical tests distributed during the Operating Systems Laboratory. These practical tests consist of three graded exercises, which will propose the use of UNIX/Linux system calls for process creation and communication in C language. Students must submit a modified version that meets all requirements within a specified time limit; versions submitted after the deadline or not meeting all requirements will be considered invalid. Each test is evaluated with a maximum of 11 points. The final grade is the sum of the scores obtained in each evaluated laboratory, with a maximum total of 33 points. If the final grade is not sufficient, students can take a practical exam on all laboratory topics during the exam periods; a score of 32 or higher results in 30 cum laude.
